observation: Citrus appears in four of five primaries; tea and spice recur in alternates; herb overlaps kitchen cilantro. The dairy base is a single outlier.
tension_or_risk: Sharing may mean sameness; the dairy drink shares nothing and carries a cold-chain burden.
future_test_question: Which bases can one citrus, tea or spice stock serve without tasting repetitive?

observation: Kitchen limes, cilantro and tamarind could feed both food and drinks.
tension_or_risk: Drink demand could compete with the kitchen for the same fresh items; unverified.
future_test_question: Does shared sourcing reduce waste in a timed trial, or create shortages?

observation: Pale clear citrus drinks look alike; the ruby tea and the cream dairy drink stand apart.
tension_or_risk: Three similar pale drinks could blur; no shared glass or garnish rule is set.
future_test_question: Do guests tell the drinks apart by sight on a mocked-up tray, using blank signage?

observation: Roles differ in theory: cleanse, aroma bridge, acid and tannin, savory reset, cooling cream. The chicken and gobi coolers overlap most.
tension_or_risk: Lime-forward fruit and lime-saline coolers may be redundant; tamarind appears in the goat tea and the gobi alternate.
future_test_question: Blind-taste the two coolers beside their dishes; can tasters tell them apart or prefer one?

observation: Most bases are cold infusions or mixes; dairy and warm tea need different handling.
tension_or_risk: Five bases with different prep may exceed small-team capacity; unmeasured.
future_test_question: Timed prep log: how much labour does each base need per service?

observation: Fresh fruit, herbs and dairy are the likely waste points; tea and dry botanicals less so.
tension_or_risk: Low-volume drinks may spoil before use; no demand data exists.
future_test_question: Waste log in a small trial: which bases go unsold, and why?

observation: Each drink has a plain descriptive label tied to a dish.
tension_or_risk: Five NA listings plus beers may clutter a short menu and confuse guests; unverified.
future_test_question: Can guests read the pairing list quickly and choose without help on a mocked menu?

observation: Fruit, herb and lime availability may vary; tea, spice and tamarind are steadier.
tension_or_risk: The fruit cooler depends most on season; recipe drift could erode the pairing.
future_test_question: Which drinks need a seasonal substitute, and does the pairing still hold?

observation: Tea, saline and citrus drinks may suit batches; dairy and carbonated drinks are harder.
tension_or_risk: Batch safety, shelf life and fizz loss are unanswered and belong to a food-safety professional.
future_test_question: What can be safely batched ahead, per a food-safety professional, and for how long?

observation: Pour-to-order drinks from chilled bases should be quick; warm tea and fresh garnish add steps.
tension_or_risk: Five different glasses and garnishes may slow a busy service; unmeasured.
future_test_question: Time a simulated rush: does a mixed order of NA drinks slow the pass?

dimension: whether five distinct NA drinks is operationally reasonable or testing should reduce them
observation: Five may be too many; two coolers overlap and tea recurs. Testing could consider fewer bases serving several dishes.
tension_or_risk: Reducing may weaken dish-specific pairing; keeping five may overload prep. Do not decide without trial data.
future_test_question: Test a reduced set against the full set: do guests and cooks prefer fewer drinks with shared bases?

dimension: one NASHA system or five separate drinks
observation: Shared themes of acid, spice and plain labels give some unity; the dairy drink and the NA beer category break the pattern.
tension_or_risk: Without a common rule on glass, garnish and sweetness, the set reads as five ideas, not one system.
future_test_question: Does a tasting panel see a common NASHA character across the five, or just five drinks?

observation: Each dish has a beer and an NA option with equal pairing logic in the existing hypotheses.
tension_or_risk: NA could be placed second by default; any NA beer category needs a qualified brewer and an alcohol attorney for strength and labelling.
future_test_question: Do guests choose NA pairings as readily as beer when both are shown equally? No evidence yet.
